A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same patch-level training work. All pages, equations, tables and figures support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments, benchmark evaluations, instruction-following results and sensitivity analyses in Section 3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds an architecture ablation in Section 3.7 and Table 5.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains averaged token embeddings, a shared prediction head, next-patch training and subsequent token-level adaptation. v2 tests additional mapping layers as architectural alternatives but explicitly retains the original method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the Pile, WikiText-103, the same six zero-shot benchmarks, GPT4 Alpaca and MT-Bench. The 60B-token multi-epoch experiment already appears in v1; the new architecture ablation introduces no dataset, domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 5 compares the original patch-training architecture against three internal alternatives: +InputMap, +OutputMap and +Both. The comparator sets in the existing benchmark experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.7 adds an architecture comparison using 90B training tokens, a 370M-parameter model, batch size 512K and lambda = 1/2, evaluating both patch-level and final token-level perplexity. Existing benchmark protocols, including the 60B-token, six-epoch experiment, are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new architecture ablation tests whether learned input and output mappings improve patch modeling and subsequent transfer. It complements the retained context-length, scaling, patch-size, training-fraction and neuron-activation analyses; the multi-epoch results are reorganized rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new architecture table introduces no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds patch perplexities of 159.17, 146.93, 99.48 and 86.50, and final token perplexities of 11.46, 11.63, 11.50 and 12.33, respectively for Transformer, +InputMap, +OutputMap and +Both. These show better patch fitting but worse final token performance for the alternatives. Existing tables and result figures retain their findings and values.

T1.justification: The patch-embedding definition, training loss and cost-reduction expression remain unchanged. v2's introductory C ≈ 6ND formula provides standard compute-accounting motivation rather than a substantive theoretical development; no new proof or formal guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that patch-level training followed by token-level adaptation can halve training costs while maintaining comparable performance across 370M–2.7B models. The revised information-density framing does not change the central contribution or empirical claim.

C2.justification: Section 3.7 explicitly discusses the loss of within-patch token order and interprets the new ablation as showing that lower patch loss need not improve final token performance. The neuron-activation discussion also expands its interpretation toward unused model capacity. Existing scalability qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new ablation's input and output mapping dimensions, token-level output construction, removal of extra parameters during transfer, and experimental settings. The main implementation recipe, optimizer settings, tokenizer and source-code access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Anagnostidis et al., Beyer et al., Muennighoff et al. and Nawrot et al., while removing four introductory references. Related work expands connections to changing visual patch sizes and resolution. Positioning against model growth shifts from potential joint application toward preserving the full parameter set.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract and introductory motivation around compute and information density, promotes existing multi-epoch material into Section 3.3, and edits the discussion and conclusion. The overall section structure and most method and experimental exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 and relocates existing displays as the text reflows: Figures 6–7 move from page 7 to page 8, and Figure 8 moves from page 8 to page 9. The eight existing figures and Tables 1–4 are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: The new architecture ablation supplies evidence for a previously largely qualitative design rationale: adding both mappings lowers patch perplexity from 159.17 to 86.50 but worsens final token perplexity from 11.46 to 12.33. Expanded related-work context also helps. These are limited gains; the main evaluations remain unchanged, and stronger claims about preserving full model capabilities receive no new comparison against model-growth methods.
